Nevertheless, with recent profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 54% [E32], the company is beginning to outperform expectations even as the stock remains at just 7% of its 52-week range [E4].

This lack of revenue is compounded by negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -3.91 Cr [E20, E21], resulting in a dismal cash conversion rate of -1.00x [E19]. Furthermore, the reported earnings are of questionable quality as they include Rs 4.43 Cr in other income [E35], while the return on equity of -5.85% and ROCE of 2.3% both significantly trail sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Despite a small market capitalization of ₹ 11.2 Cr [E2], the business is burdened by substantial borrowings of Rs 114.29 Cr [E23], and its EV/EBITDA of 29.37x is more than double the sector benchmark of 13.11x [E10]. Investors should also note that the promoter holding is low at 31.5% [E34], and the stock has lost 50% of its value over the last year [E16]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 87 per share against a market price of Rs 15 [E28], yielding a massive margin of safety of 82.8% [E29]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price already incorrectly prices in a -21.9% earnings contraction, completely ignoring the multi-year profit uptrend and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 18% [E14, E30, E38].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 87 per share against a market price of Rs 15 [E28, E29]. However, that theoretical margin of safety ignores severe fundamental deterioration, notably a compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months of -100% [E12]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of cash flow strain is invalid because operating and free cash flow plummeted to Rs -3.91 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a cash conversion ratio of -1.00x [E19, E20, E21], rendering past liquidity figures from Mar 2025 [E22] stale. The low share price—sitting at just 7% of its 52-week range [E4]—reflects profound underlying risks, including a negative return on equity of -5.85% [E8] and an inflated EV/EBITDA of 29.37x that vastly exceeds the sector benchmark of 13.11x [E10]. Additionally, reported profits are artificially propped up by non-operating sources, specifically inclusion of other income worth Rs 4.43 Cr [E35], while earnings growth actively decelerates [E40]. Finally, the heavy debt burden of Rs 114.29 Cr [E23] combined with low promoter holdings of only 31.5% [E34] exposes minority shareholders to severe structural vulnerability.
